authority: SESSION 26 brief, in the repository author's own words: 'Enable automatic implementation only for explicitly approved low-risk categories. Examples may include: source metadata maintenance; non-substantive retrieval metadata; verified source URL corrections; machine-derived fields where canonical source is unchanged; clearly governed metadata changes… Do not allow substantive legal content to auto-merge.'
rationale: The five categories protocol section 20 names, and no others. The path allowlist is the real narrowing: data/sources.json because the first three categories are about that file and nothing else, and docs/ because docs/AUTONOMY-POLICY.md Class A already permits reports and proposals there with no approval at all — this grant does not widen that, it puts the four validators, the browser suite, a trace and a verified rollback in front of it. The field allowlist is what keeps substantive legal content out of an enabled category: tier, role, supports, last_verified, verification_note, requires_verification and reference_gap are on the never-automatic list, so an edit described as bookkeeping that in fact re-tiers a source is refused by reading the operation target rather than by trusting the description. Six months rather than open-ended: an authorization nobody revisits is an authorization nobody owns, and the expiry is a judgement this session made rather than something the brief stated.
